seo.title: Benchmarks — OpenMixer
seo.description: DSP load, memory, xruns and time to add for the same plugins on plugin-hostd, omx-clap-host and mod-host, measured on a Raspberry Pi 5.

hero.title: The same plugins on three hosts
hero.lede: Each scenario runs the same plugins at the same sample rate and buffer size on each host. The load is the DSP load of the JACK server that drives them, read while the scenario plays. Levels, where this page gives them, are measured digitally at JACK ports.
hero.reproduce: The bench harness in the plugin-hostd repository writes the runs on this page and repeats them on any machine.

hostMeaning.H1: The CLAP host driven directly through the mod-host protocol on its own port. All plugins share its one process.
hostMeaning.H2: The plugin daemon with omx-clap-host as its worker. Plugins run in isolated workers, and a chain is one worker.
hostMeaning.H3: The mod-host program as Zynthian ships it. LV2 plugins only.
hostMeaning.H4: One jalv process per plugin, the way plugins ran on a Zynthian before.

variant.H2_chain: plugin-hostd, chain built after the adds

benchmarks.noRun: No run is committed for this machine class.

lowest.title: Lowest buffer without an xrun
lowest.lede: A buffer is the short block of audio a host processes at a time, counted in frames. The host must finish each block before the next one is due; if it does not, the sound glitches, and that glitch is an xrun. The smaller the buffer, the less time audio waits before it comes out, so a smaller buffer is a lower latency. This table gives, for each host, the smallest buffer at which every repeat ran with no xrun, read from the rows measured below.
lowest.unit: Milliseconds are the frames divided by the rate. A size counts only if the row ran and the highest repeat had 0 xruns. Only the sizes in the measured set are tried.
lowest.none: None of the measured sizes; the smallest measured is {frames} frames ({ms} ms)
lowest.quarter: A quarter of the buffer of {ref}

method.title: How it was measured
method.text: {machine}, governor {governor}, a private JACK server on the dummy driver at {rate}, {frames} frames. Every figure is the median of {repeats} repeats, with the lowest and the highest repeat beside it. Nothing is rounded; a figure is shown as the harness wrote it.
method.versions: Rows marked omx-clap-core ran on the version named in the row. The omx-clap-host rows ran on omx-clap-core 0.26.3 and the plugin-hostd rows on 0.26.4, because on 0.26.3 the plugin-hostd chains did not form (see the rows that did not pass).

scenario.cvp24: 24 plugins, CLAP builds (Calf as LV2; mod-host runs the LV2 builds)
scenario.cvp24-lv2: The same 24 plugins, LV2 builds on every host

acceptance.failed: the host did not run the scenario
acceptance.xruns: an xrun in at least one repeat

family.lede: Each cell shows the median DSP load, the proportional memory (PSS) of the host processes and the xruns, each with the lowest and highest repeat. A cell that fails acceptance is marked and stays in the table.
family.unit: DSP load in percent of the audio cycle, as reported by the JACK server. PSS in MB. Acceptance is 0 xruns in every repeat.

failing.title: Rows that did not pass
failing.lede: Every row of this day's runs that failed to run or had an xrun in a repeat. They are the results too; none is left out.
failing.none: No row of this run failed.
failing.cause: On omx-clap-core 0.26.3 none of the plugin-hostd chains formed: Calf and the DPF plugins set the flush-to-zero bit of the FPCR register when their library is opened, and the register guard took it for theirs and moved each such plugin to a worker of its own. 0.26.4 logs that change and no longer isolates the plugin for it.
failing.cost: One worker per plugin is the heavy mode: 24 processes and 24 JACK clients on four cores. It is not the default.

stress.title: Rows under stress
stress.none: Not measured. Every row of this run ran with no added load.

add.title: How long it takes to add the plugins
add.lede: Cold is a host just started, then every plugin of the set added, until the last one runs. Warm is the same plugins added to a host that is already running. The lowest median of a row is in bold; the range is the lowest and highest repeat.
add.unit: Milliseconds, median of the repeats. Warm rows are chains of omx comp, delay and drive in their LV2 builds, so every host runs the same plugins.

instruments.title: One instrument, 1, 8 and 16 notes
instruments.lede: DSP load and PSS for one instance. The standalone rows run as their own JACK programs, as Zynthian runs them, and do not go through either host.
instruments.name: Instrument
instruments.unit: Percent of the audio cycle, then MB, then xruns as median and highest repeat. Peak is measured digitally at the JACK ports.

profile.title: The worker's audio thread, 24 plugins in one chain
profile.lede: Shares of the samples of the audio thread of the plugin-hostd worker, from perf. The profiled library was built on the Pi from the same tag, because the shipped one has no symbols; a share can move by a point.
